title: Plimpton 322 has more than one reading

body: Plimpton 322 is an Old Babylonian clay tablet. Popular accounts have described it as a trigonometric table, sometimes with a certainty the evidence does not force. Eleanor Robson's 2001 paper in Historia Mathematica is titled "Neither Sherlock Holmes nor Babylon: A Reassessment of Plimpton 322." The title marks a reassessment of a detective-style reconstruction and of what the tablet shows about Babylonian mathematics. This card does not replace her argument with a new decoding of the numbers. It records that a specialist reassessment exists and that the textbook story of the tablet is contested. The Pythagorean relation itself is securely in Euclid's Elements, a Greek text from many centuries later. Presence of related number patterns on a Babylonian tablet does not mean Babylonian scribes were doing Greek geometry under another name.
